questions.label: B1(a)
questions.question_text: PET ID is the primary key of the PETS table. State what is meant by a primary key.
questions.mark_scheme:
Award the mark for: A field that uniquely identifies each record (no two records have the same value).
Check / do not accept: A "key field" with no explanation: no mark.

questions.label: B1(b)
questions.question_text: PET ID is the primary key of the PETS table. Identify the foreign key in the PETS table.
questions.mark_scheme: Award the mark for: OWNER ID.

questions.label: B2(1)
questions.question_text: State the type of relationship between the OWNERS table and the PETS table. Explain your answer.
questions.mark_scheme:
Award the mark for: One-to-many.
Check / do not accept: Many-to-one only if the explanation is correct.

questions.label: B2(2)
questions.question_text: State the type of relationship between the OWNERS table and the PETS table. Explain your answer.
questions.mark_scheme: Award the mark for: One owner can have many pets, but each pet has only one owner.

questions.label: B3(1)
questions.question_text: Explain one advantage of storing this data in three linked tables rather than in one table.
questions.mark_scheme: Award the mark for: Data is stored once / not repeated (less redundancy), e.g. an owner's name and mobile are stored once, not with every pet or appointment.

questions.label: B3(2)
questions.question_text: Explain one advantage of storing this data in three linked tables rather than in one table.
questions.mark_scheme: Award the mark for: So it is changed in only one place / fewer inconsistencies / less storage space.

questions.label: B4(a)(1)
questions.question_text: Referential integrity is enforced in this database. Explain why referential integrity is enforced between the PETS table and the APPOINTMENTS table.
questions.mark_scheme: Award the mark for: An appointment cannot be entered for a PET ID that does not exist in PETS (or a pet with appointments cannot be deleted).

questions.label: B4(a)(2)
questions.question_text: Referential integrity is enforced in this database. Explain why referential integrity is enforced between the PETS table and the APPOINTMENTS table.
questions.mark_scheme: Award the mark for: This stops records that are not linked (orphan records) / reduces data entry errors.

questions.label: B4(b)
questions.question_text: Referential integrity is enforced in this database. State which of the three tables must have its data entered first.
questions.mark_scheme: Award the mark for: OWNERS.

questions.label: B5(a)

questions.mark_scheme:
Award the mark for: Yes/No (accept Boolean).
Check / do not accept: Text: no mark.

questions.label: B5(b)
questions.question_text: The MOBILE field has the data type Text. Give one reason why it is not stored as a Number.
questions.mark_scheme: Award the mark for: A Number field would remove the leading 0 / it is not used in calculations / it may contain + or spaces.

questions.label: B5(c)
questions.question_text: Suggest a suitable field size for the MOBILE field.
questions.mark_scheme:
Award the mark for: 10 (accept 10–15).
Check / do not accept: 255, 50 or default: no mark.

questions.mark_scheme: Award the mark for: Users could type a value that is not in the list (e.g. a misspelt vet name).

questions.label: B6(b)(2)
questions.question_text: The VET lookup list has Limit to List set to Yes. Explain one problem that could happen if Limit to List was set to No.
questions.mark_scheme: Award the mark for: So those records would be missed by queries / data would be inconsistent.

questions.label: B8(a)

questions.mark_scheme: Award the mark for: To search using more than one criterion / to combine conditions.
